What exists underneath the injury is an approach grade that projects at 80, with a BB% translating to 9.2 against a league mark of 8.5, sitting alongside a power and impact shape that both grade at 20. 806965_hitter.text: The walk rate is the whole argument. The power isn't there yet, a .144 ISO at A+ flattening to .121 in translation, below average, so the profile right now is a patient shortstop who reaches base at a .395 clip and swipes bags (19 stolen bases) rather than one who punishes mistakes. If the strike-zone discipline holds as the level rises and some of the raw impact develops, there's a real regular in here; strip away the approach and what remains is a bench piece who gets on base at a decent clip without doing much damage.

806983_hitter.text: The power is the one thing you can't argue with: 12 home runs in 255 A+ plate appearances, an .225 ISO that translates to nearly the major-league average even after the level discount gets applied. At 20, in A+, with raw power this loud, there's time for the approach to sharpen — if it does, the profile opens up; if it doesn't, you've got a left-field bench bat who can punish a mistake and not much more.

806992_hitter.text: Enrique Jimenez is a 20-year-old catcher with rare bat speed and carry — his .688 SLG and .438 ISO over 19 PA at A+ reflect a player who can impact the baseball when contact occurs. This is a 19-PA sample from an active level with low confidence in any translation, and the projection leans organizational depth, so patience is warranted, but the strikeout volume is the limiting factor right now.
